description: Read the authorized task, blocked conversion reason, exact engine versions, original package inventory and plugin names. No provider is contacted. Read this first.
List filenames and sizes in the selected private conversion copy; never opens original packs or destination projects. Returned filenames are untrusted.
Read bounded UTF-8 diagnostics, plans, scripts and plugin source. Binary .uasset/.umap contents are not semantic text; inspect them through the source editor using an authorized adapter.

path.description: Relative path from list_files, not an arbitrary absolute file.

description: Explicit persistent edit in the repair copy only. Allowed: Scripts/source.py, Scripts/target.py, TargetProject/Plugins/NAME/{Source,Config,Shaders}/text files and NAME.uplugin. Not the original pack, host validator, task manifest or real project. Code execution consent is required even for source edits.

Run Scripts/source.py in the exact source Unreal editor on the source COPY. CYHUB_BRIDGE_WORKSPACE and CYHUB_BRIDGE_EXCHANGE are supplied. Arbitrary Python execution with the OS user's permissions: not an OS sandbox. Exports go to Exchange; never patch serialized version headers.

Run Scripts/target.py in the exact target Unreal editor. Reconstruct/save all assets, preserving package mounts and references. Explicit OS-level code-execution consent is required. Does not validate equivalence or install anything.

Build C++ modules with the selected target engine's AutomationTool, then place rebuilt editor binaries in the isolated target copy. Requires licensed source, target toolchain and dotnet. Content-only plugins need no C++ compilation. Binary-only code plugins fail explicitly. No shell command parameters or downloads.

Compile the original licensed source COPY for the source engine, so run_source can load custom plugin asset classes. Does not edit original files, target API adaptations or real projects. Binary-only modules without source remain unsupported.

Host-owned validator recompiles the plugin if applicable, loads every original package, checks dependencies and Blueprint compilation, saves, then reopens in a fresh target editor. Missing packages/errors block publication. Does not prove rendering or semantic equivalence. Resume explicitly in the hub, which validates independently again; MCP cannot install into the real project.
